title: Module Docstring: Closing the Parent's Open Future Work
content: The parent file (QBinomial namespace) built the Gaussian binomial coefficient qBinomial q n k from the q-Pascal recurrence C_q(n+1,k+1)=q^{k+1}C_q(n,k+1)+C_q(n,k), proved the boundary/vanishing lemmas, and established only the m=0 and n=0 base cases of q-Vandermonde — leaving the full inductive identity as 'Open future work #1'. This file proves it. The headline is the q-Vandermonde convolution C_q(m+n,r)=Σ_k q^{(m-k)(r-k)} C_q(m,k) C_q(n,r-k), valid over any commutative ring (subtraction q^j−1 needs additive inverses). The whole argument hinges on one new lemma — the absorption identity (★) — proved first and applied term-by-term in the induction.

title: Setup: Importing the Gallery's q-Binomial API over a CommRing
content: Imports the parent BinomialTheoremOQ02OQ02OQ01 (opening QBinomial) — Mathlib has no Gaussian binomial API as of v4.26, so the gallery supplies it. GeomSum provides the geometric-sum identity (∑q^i)(q−1)=q^n−1 used in the absorption base case. Everything is stated for a generic [CommRing R]: q ranges over R, but the indices m, n, r, k are natural numbers, so q-binomials are genuine polynomials in q evaluated in R.

title: The Absorption Identity (★) — the Crux Lemma
content: qBinomial_absorption states (q^{k+1}−1)·C_q(m,k+1) = (q^{m-k}−1)·C_q(m,k) for all k. This is the q-analog of the classical absorption relation (k+1)·C(m,k+1) = (m−k)·C(m,k): the integer factors (k+1) and (m−k) become the q-integers [k+1]_q·(q−1)=q^{k+1}−1 and [m−k]_q·(q−1)=q^{m-k}−1. Isolating this single identity is what turns the otherwise intimidating double-sum reconciliation of q-Vandermonde into a one-line termwise cancellation.

title: Proving Absorption by Induction on m
content: Induction on m. Base m=0: C_q(0,k+1)=0 and q^{0-k}=q^0=1 makes the right factor zero, so simp closes it. Inductive step splits on k: for k=0 the identity becomes (q−1)·C_q(m+1,1)=q^{m+1}−1, discharged by the geometric-sum closed form C_q(m+1,1)=∑q^i and geom_sum_mul. For k=j+1, expand both q-binomials by q-Pascal (qBinomial_succ_succ), then case-split on j<m vs j≥m: the generic branch telescopes q^{m-j}=q^{m-(j+1)}·q and closes by linear_combination of the two induction hypotheses; the degenerate branch uses that both q-binomials vanish (qBinomial_eq_zero_of_lt) so both sides are 0.
mathContext: Base: $(q-1)\binom{m+1}{1}_q = (q-1)\sum_{i<m+1}q^i = q^{m+1}-1$. Step uses q-Pascal and natural-subtraction case split.

title: The q-Vandermonde Statement and Induction Skeleton
content: qVandermonde proves C_q(m+n,r)=Σ_{k∈range(r+1)} q^{(m-k)(r-k)} C_q(m,k) C_q(n,r-k) by induction on n. The base case n=0 is exactly the parent's qVandermonde_zero_right. The inductive step further cases on r: r=0 is trivial (simp), and the real work is r=s+1, where the q-Pascal expansions on both sides must be reconciled. Note the sum runs over range(r+1), but natural-number subtraction makes every out-of-range term (k>m or r−k>n) vanish automatically — no explicit range guards are needed.

title: Inductive Step: q-Pascal Expansion and Boundary Peeling
content: For r=s+1: rewrite m+(n+1)=(m+n)+1, expand C_q(m+n+1,s+1) by q-Pascal, and substitute the induction hypothesis at both r=s+1 and r=s. On the target side, expand each inner C_q(n+1,s+1−k) by q-Pascal (hRsum) splitting it into a q^{s+1-k}-weighted 'high' part over C_q(n,s+1−k) and a 'low' part over C_q(n,s−k). Both sides then have their k=s+1 boundary term peeled off via sum_range_succ: on the right it reduces (hRpeel) to C_q(m,s+1); on the left (hLpeel) to q^{s+1}·C_q(m,s+1). This aligns both sides as sums of the same shape plus boundary terms.
mathContext: $\binom{n+1}{s+1-k}_q = q^{s+1-k}\binom{n}{s+1-k}_q + \binom{n}{s-k}_q$ (q-Pascal), applied inside the convolution sum.

title: Reconciliation: One Index Shift, Then Termwise Cancellation by Absorption
content: The heart of the proof. The 'high' sum (hHQ) has its k=0 term vanish, so it reindexes (sum_range_succ') from range(s+1) down to range s. The 'low' sum (hLQ) has its k=s term peeled, also landing on range s, leaving the boundary factor (q^{m-s}−1)·C_q(m,s). Now both sums run over range s with a common C_q(n,s−k) factor, and the key lemma hterm shows each aligned pair cancels to 0: for k<m this is a linear_combination of three exponent-bookkeeping identities (hpow1–hpow3) and the absorption identity hab at k; for k≥m the q-binomials vanish. The leftover boundary terms are reconciled by the absorption identity habs at k=s. The final linear_combination −hHQ−hLQ−hHL0+habs assembles all pieces into the goal.
mathContext: Each aligned term vanishes via $(q^{k+1}-1)\binom{m}{k+1}_q=(q^{m-k}-1)\binom{m}{k}_q$; leftover boundary $=$ absorption at $k=s$.

title: Classical Vandermonde at q=1
content: vandermonde_classical specializes q=1: every power weight q^{(m-k)(r-k)} becomes 1, and qBinomial_at_one identifies C_1(n,k)=C(n,k) (the ordinary binomial). The general identity collapses to the classical Vandermonde convolution C(m+n,r)=Σ_k C(m,k)·C(n,r−k), cast into R. This confirms the chosen power-weight convention q^{(m-k)(r-k)} is the correct one: it is the unique exponent compatible with both the gallery's q-Pascal recurrence and the q=1 limit.
